title: Verification request
description: A set of declared proof obligations to discharge against a xorq catalog (ADR-0001 §6). The producer of a data answer emits this; pi-xorq-check (or the xorq_verify tool) discharges it into a certificate. Declaring obligations here is the strong path: the claim→expression binding is given, not inferred by the verifier.

catalog_path.description: Path to the re-runnable xorq catalog.

expressions.description: Declared aliases and their lineage; grounds the provenance check for obligations that carry requires_sources.

reply_values.description: Every surface value asserted by the answer; an uncovered value forces COULD-NOT-VERIFY (the coverage audit).

catalog_witnesses.description: Persist each DISCHARGED witness as a composed, re-runnable `verify-<id>` catalog entry (the certificate reports each as witness_ref). The xorq_verify tool defaults this to true; pass false for a throwaway check that should leave no trace in the catalog.

no_local_sources.description: No-fabricated-inputs policy. When true, every obligation's witness alias must be built from re-fetchable data only, grounded in the alias's ACTUAL op-tree (not a declared list). It enforces two checks, both fail-closed to COULD-NOT-DISCHARGE: `remote_sources` — every leaf must be a Read from a remote URL (http/https/s3/gs/...); a local/scratch path, or an in-memory/hand-built table (surfaced as a `<in-memory>` leaf, even when joined to a real source), is rejected. `no_magic_constants` — no non-unit numeric literal may be hardcoded in the alias's arithmetic (a fabricated population/price typed into a mutate); unit scales like 100 or 100000 are allowed, so a data value must come from a joined column. The operator can force the policy on regardless of this field via the PI_XORQ_NO_LOCAL_SOURCES env var.

obligation.description: A declared claim plus its WITNESS SITE. Terminology: the producer declares the site — `on` (a declared alias), `population` (a clean restriction of it), and the predicate. The witness itself — the expression that is re-run to discharge the claim — is SYNTHESIZED by the checker from that declaration (the certificate discloses it as witness_code and, when persisted, witness_ref). The producer never writes the check; a mis-declared site can weaken what is claimed, never forge how it is verified. The one exception is an ungrounded scalar, whose full expression the producer supplies via `expression`.

kind.description: The predicate shape. Every kind listed here discharges end-to-end. Kinds without a discharge rule (compare/metric/metadata/provenance, ADR-0005 modes) are deliberately NOT in this contract — the checker still fails closed on an unknown kind, but the schema only advertises what verifies today.

surface.description: The value verbatim as written in the answer, e.g. "17,875". Required for the value kinds (it is the claimed value). Optional for a `table`, whose content is its grid (predicate.rows) — there `surface` is at most a label.

tolerance.description: Decimal string ε for numeric kinds.

on.description: A DECLARED alias the checker composes the witness on — the site's base. The witness itself is synthesized; this only names where it lives.

population.description: The POPULATION the witness ranges over: a restriction of the alias, e.g. source.filter(source.markets >= 25). Combine conditions by CHAINING filters — source.filter(a).filter(b) for AND — never source.filter((a) & (b)): the safe evaluator rejects bitwise &/|. For argmax/argmin/count/membership/table the checker builds the canonical ranking/aggregation ON TOP of this population and recomputes the extremum over the SAME population, so the judgment and its cross-check both come from the witness. Must be a clean restriction (a filter): no join, set op, or limit — those would fabricate or pre-narrow the population and are rejected. Empty/omitted = the whole alias. Validated over its op-tree: selection-only, non-circular, rooted on the alias.

expression.description: UNGROUNDED SCALAR ONLY: the full expression whose cell is the claimed value, e.g. source.aggregate(total=source.n.sum()) — the one kind whose witness the checker cannot synthesize. Ignored for the synthesized kinds (they fail closed rather than evaluate producer code as the witness). Validated over its op-tree like `population`.

select.description: Column whose cell equals `surface` in the witness result.

entity_col.description: Column the value is grounded to (the row must be this entity's).

entity_val.description: The entity the value belongs to, e.g. "ATL".

metric_col.description: For argmax/argmin: the column the extremum ranges over (the checker recomputes max/min over this column to discharge maximality — the quantifier is never declared, always recomputed). Required when `select` is not itself the ranked numeric column, e.g. an entity claim selecting `origin` ranked by `n`.

measures.description: Semantic-model scalar: measure names from the alias's own BSL model. The checker SYNTHESIZES the witness itself (source.ls.builder.query(...)) — never set `expression` alongside; set `select` to the claimed measure. Ranges over the whole model: `population` is rejected.

dimensions.description: Semantic-model scalar: optional dimension names to slice `measures` by (BSL model names). Ground a sliced value's row with entity_col/entity_val.

columns.description: table kind: the columns compared against the witness grid (and, for a ranking, their display order).

rows.description: table kind: the claimed rows, each an object of {column: value-as-written}. Compared to the witness result — positionally when ordered, else as an order-insensitive set.

ordered.description: table kind: true = ranking/row (positional, needs metric_col to order); false = set (order-insensitive; the witness population defines membership). Default true.

value_types.description: table kind: per-column value types, {column: {kind, tolerance}}; columns not listed use the obligation's value_type.

requires_sources.description: Sources the witness alias's lineage must cover (checked against expressions[].lineage).
